title: Segmentation-driven console request triage and cost-estimate matrix
creator: Lena Kim
description:
Background: We continue to receive a high volume of enterprise console/reporting requests that vary widely in complexity — from simple per-workspace CSV exports to multi-tenant, scheduled billing reconciliations and cross-workspace analytics. Current intake lacks structured signals for expected engineering effort, token cost exposure, and SLA tiering. That causes long TTR, unpredictable prioritization decisions, and occasional scope creep when requests surface heavy telemetry joins or long historical windows.

Objective: Define a segmentation-driven triage matrix and an automated cost-estimate model (prototype) to: 1) classify incoming requests into 3 priority lanes (Fast-track, Engineering-scheduled, Solution-engagement), 2) provide a near-real-time estimated implementation score (effort, infra cost delta, data sensitivity), and 3) return clear acceptance criteria and routing recommendations to the requestor.

Scope:
- Intake fields & UX: propose required fields for the Console request form (e.g., workspace scope, retention window, query complexity, export frequency, required SLA, recipients).
- Segmentation rules: tenant size bands (small/medium/large), telemetry volume buckets, query complexity heuristics, and security sensitivity flags.
- Cost estimator: simple model that combines estimated token generation/embedding units + export frequency + compute hours to produce a conservative monthly delta in USD for hosted and dedicated customers.
- Routing & SLAs: mapping from segmentation + cost delta to recommended route (self-serve template, PM review, solutions engineering + dedicated SOW).
- Developer handoff artifacts: PRD fields, example SQL/Looker queries, sample acceptance criteria for each lane.

Success criteria:
- Reduce average triage time from request -> assigned owner to <72 hours for high-impact enterprise asks.
- >60% of incoming requests receive an actionable routing recommendation (lane + estimate) without follow-up.
- Engineering rework (scope misunderstandings) drops by 30% on processed requests.

Out of scope for this ticket: building a fully-automated estimator backend or changing billing. This ticket produces the matrix, intake schema, and a spreadsheet prototype estimator and ownership plan for engineering to build iteratively.
acceptance_criteria: Draft intake schema published in Confluence
Segmentation matrix with explicit rule examples and thresholds
Spreadsheet prototype cost estimator with adjustable knobs (frequency, window, token rate)
Routing table mapping segments to lanes and recommended SLA/response targets
Stakeholder sign-off from Support, Sales Engineering, and Security
comments: 2026-03-02 -- Miguel Ortega: Kickoff complete. Met with Support and SE to collect 25 recent enterprise asks. Noted three common failure modes: large historical windows, multi-workspace joins, and scheduled delivery frequency. Action: assemble sample set of 10 representative requests.

2026-03-04 -- Asha Patel (Support): Shared anonymized request corpus and customer impact notes. Confirmed that customers are most sensitive to delivery cadence and cost transparency. Asked for a 'ballpark cost' field on the intake form.

2026-03-06 -- Design review with Priya Shah: Proposed intake form wireframes (fields: workspace_id, expected rows, retention_window_months, export_format, cadence, recipients, data_sensitivity_level). Priya recommends collapsible advanced options to reduce friction.

2026-03-07 -- Engineering sync (ENG-88412): Eng raised concerns about token cost estimation accuracy for queries that trigger reranking/embedding pipelines. Decided to include 'estimation confidence' and a conservative multiplier for P0 routing.
2026-03-08 -- Draft segmentation matrix posted: Small (<10k active MAU), Medium (10k-200k), Large (>200k) + telemetry buckets (low/medium/high). Request feedback from Sales by 2026-03-12.
2026-03-09 -- Francisco Ruiz (SE): Requested a 'data residency' and 'KMS/HSM required' flag to properly route to Private deployments. Added to intake schema.

2026-03-10 -- PM review: Incorporated feedback and updated prototype spreadsheet (link below). Preparing stakeholder review session on 2026-03-12. Next step: finalize thresholds and owner matrix for SLOs.
open_questions: What threshold should move a request from 'Engineering-scheduled' to 'Solution-engagement' (SOW)? Suggestion: >$2k/mo estimated infra delta or >3 cross-workspace joins.
Do we expose the cost estimate to customers on first request or only internally during triage?
Should scheduled exports (daily) always be escalated for billing review regardless of size?
Can we reliably compute token-equivalent cost for existing ad-hoc queries without running a dry-run?
next_steps: Run workshop 2026-03-12 with Sales, Support, Security, and Eng to finalize lane thresholds
Publish Confluence PRD and intake form specs by 2026-03-16
Hand off spreadsheet prototype and routing rules to ENG (ENG-88412) for a minimal API to power the estimator
Pilot the intake with 5 upcoming enterprise requests in March and collect feedback
